name: 44594-longdecode-7b-1gpu
hardware: 1x NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of an a3 node, --gres=gpu:1), sm90.
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1, one vLLM engine on one GPU.
architecture: Dense transformer decoder, 7.6B parameters in bf16 (~15 GB of safetensors); the rest is in the checkpoint's own config.json.
load_profile: concurrent (CLOSED loop), streams=128, warmup 10%, cooldown 10%, bounded at 450 requests with a 3600 s safety cap, static seed 44594.
workload: synthetic `synthetic_text`, single turn, no shared prefix, `temperature: 0.0`. Prompt ~1000 tokens and output ~5000, each drawn INTEGER-UNIFORM over +/-20% -- prompts in [800, 1200], outputs in [4000, 6000]. `ignore_eos` and a hard `max_tokens` are forced, so the sampled output length is what is actually generated. The engine tokenizes the rendered prompt, so reported prompt counts land a few tokens off the band; that is not drift.
purpose: A long-form report writer on one GPU, where a 7B model turns brief prompts into multi-thousand-token drafts for 128 concurrent users.
launch:
# The serve command for this setup. Nothing here is tuned.

model: Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct

tensor-parallel-size: 1

# 16 GiB = 16 * 1024^3. PART OF THE DECLARATION, NOT A KNOB: pinning the KV cache in BYTES makes
# the block count identical on any GPU that fits the weights plus 16 GiB. Raising it is a
# different setup.
kv-cache-memory-bytes: 17179869184

max-model-len: 8192

max-num-seqs: 256

# Part of the declaration: the prompts are independent synthetic text.
enable-prefix-caching: false

gpu-memory-utilization: 0.90
